_note: Iteration-1 eval set for v0.9 → v1.0 promotion sweep. 10 cases × ~10 assertions ≈ 100+ assertions, mirroring the ai-act-high-risk methodology. Cases cover the major outcome types (consultation response, internal/external memo, public commentary EN+DE, comparative, horizon-scan, litigation, conference, skill input) and the major instrument types (Commission Guidelines draft, CJEU judgment, EDPB Guidelines, Regulation + Directive comparative, national DPA decision, draft delegated act, harmonised standard, code of conduct). Includes deliberate tests for: the automatic freshness check on drafts (case 5), the routing-to-sibling integration (case 8), the live research opt-in (case 6), and the plain-English explainer (every case).

evals.name: consultation-response-on-commission-draft-bilingual
evals.prompt: Hi, I want to submit a stakeholder consultation response to the European Commission's draft guidelines on Article 6(5) of the AI Act (high-risk classification under Article 6). The draft was published for public consultation in 2026. Our company position is that the Commission's worked example on smart thermostats (paragraphs 48-49 of the draft) is too narrow and risks creating uncertainty for borderline IoT products. Please prepare the consultation response. Audience is the Commission; stance is challenging the specific worked example while remaining constructive. Output in English. The deliverable is due in 2 weeks.
evals.expected_output: Characterisation of the document (draft Commission Guidelines under Art. 6(5) AI Act, non-binding interpretive instrument, under consultation), automatic freshness check triggered. Tailored expert prompt assembled with the nine required blocks. Consultation-response output structure (problem statement, our position, reasoning grounded in the Act, drafting suggestion). Plain-English explainer alongside. Optional execution.
assertions: Identifies the document as draft Commission Guidelines (non-binding interpretive instrument) under Art. 6(5) AI Act
Triggers the automatic freshness check for the draft before proceeding and surfaces it to the user
Names the binding force as non-binding (interpretive; cannot extend the underlying Act)
Identifies status as under consultation
Asks at most three elicitation questions, skipping any already answered in the prompt

Generates a tailored expert prompt with the nine required blocks (Role, Context, Task, Analytical framework, Specific provisions warranting scrutiny, Citation conventions, Register constraints, Output structure, Self-check protocol)
Includes a consultation-response-specific role marker and output structure
Cites Art. 6 AI Act and references the specific paragraphs (48-49) the user is challenging
Applies the dry-practitioner register (no marketing fillers, no banned vocabulary)
Produces a plain-English explainer in 150-300 words alongside the formal output
Offers the user a choice on how to integrate the explainer (executive summary, sidebar, annex, cover note, standalone)
Does not invent paragraph numbers beyond those provided by the user (anti-hallucination protocol applied)

evals.name: comparative-analysis-gdpr-art22-vs-ai-act-art50
evals.prompt: I'm preparing a thought-leadership briefing for our partners on the overlap between Article 22 GDPR (right not to be subject to automated individual decision-making) and Article 50 AI Act (transparency obligations for AI systems interacting with natural persons, including deepfake disclosure). I want a structured comparative analysis: scope of each provision, the obligations each imposes, where they overlap, where they diverge, and what a controller deploying an AI-driven decisioning system needs to do under both. Audience is our partner-level lawyers. English, ~2000 words. Please prepare the prompt and execute it.
evals.expected_output: Characterisation of two instruments side by side. Tailored prompt for a comparative analysis. Applies the cross-instrument coherence interpretive rule. Identifies the legal bases of each provision (GDPR: Art. 16 TFEU plus Art. 114 TFEU per its preamble; AI Act: Art. 114 TFEU plus Art. 16 TFEU in respect of processing of personal data) and the consequences for scope and interpretation, the controller/operator distinction, the deployer obligations under Art. 26 AI Act that interact with GDPR controller duties, and the FRIA (Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment) requirement under Art. 27 AI Act where it applies. Executes in-session and produces plain-English explainer.
assertions: Characterises Art. 22 GDPR (binding) and Art. 50 AI Act (binding) as parallel operative provisions of two Regulations

Identifies the legal bases of each provision (GDPR grounded in Art. 16 TFEU + Art. 114 TFEU; AI Act grounded in Art. 114 TFEU + Art. 16 TFEU for personal-data processing aspects) and the consequences for scope/interpretation — does NOT treat Art. 16 and Art. 114 as mutually exclusive alternatives
Generates a tailored expert prompt with the comparative-analysis output structure (scope, obligations, overlap, divergence, practical implications)
Applies the cross-instrument coherence interpretive rule from the analytical canon
Identifies the controller (GDPR) vs deployer (AI Act, Art. 26) terminological distinction and flags the translation risk

Cites Art. 26 AI Act deployer obligations explicitly — including Art. 26(1) instruction-following, Art. 26(7) Art. 22 GDPR information duty (where the deployer makes Art. 22 GDPR decisions), and Art. 27 FRIA where applicable — and explains how Art. 26 deployer duties interact with GDPR controller duties when the deployer is also a controller
Cites Art. 22 GDPR with its three-stage test (decision based solely on automated processing → legal effect or similarly significant → exceptions in Art. 22(2)) and the safeguards in Art. 22(3)
Cites Art. 50 AI Act including the deepfake disclosure obligation under Art. 50(4) and the broader transparency obligations in Art. 50(1)-(3)
Executes the prompt in-session and produces a comparative analysis of approximately 2000 words
Produces a plain-English explainer of 150-300 words alongside (hard upper bound)
Does not conflate the GDPR's data subject rights framework with the AI Act's transparency framework; surfaces the divergence

evals.name: litigation-brief-input-on-transfer-challenge

I need: (1) the operative test from Schrems II with the relevant paragraph anchors, (2) the EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 on supplementary measures, (3) how the framework decision (C(2023) 4745) addresses the deficiencies and where it does not. Audience is the court. Output in English. Citation-heavy. Please prepare the prompt — execution will happen separately under counsel review.

Tailored prompt with the litigation-brief role marker, citation-heavy depth, and the requirement to live-verify Schrems II paragraph anchors before citing.
